newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: EU GIVES S.AFRICA $20 MILLION FOR DEMOCRACY.
newsitem.headline: EU GIVES S.AFRICA $20 MILLION FOR DEMOCRACY.

text.p: The European Union on Wednesday gave South Africa 16 million ECUs ($20.3 million) in a three-year programme to help its fledgling all-race parliament.
EU ambassador to South Africa Erwan Fouere described the money as a concrete sign of the warm relations which he said would help the two sides overcome difficulties in trade negotiations.
"We cannot hide the fact that these negotiations will be difficult," Fouere told parliamentary speaker Frene Ginwala at the presentation ceremony.
"But it is precisely because of the dynamic nature of our relationship that I am convinced we will succeed in overcoming these difficulties.
"Let us hope that our respective negotiators will let themselves be inspired by this common vision," Fouere said.
South African trade officials have objected to aspects of the EU negotiating mandate on a trade pact, saying the mandate could harm South Africa's regional trade bloc partners.

Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, currently on a tour of eight European states, is lobbying there for changes to the mandate which would also exclude nearly 40 percent of South African farm products from a trade pact.

The money presented to Ginwala on Wednesday will be used on, among other things, hiring researchers for MPs, improving parliament's communication systems and researching ways to boost public participation in law-making.
